assumptions.choice: support level = Lowest(Low, 20); resistance level = Highest(High, 20)
assumptions.reason: Spec says 'minimum/maximum over the last 20 bars' without naming a series; Low/High extremes are the standard technical-analysis definition of support/resistance touch points.

assumptions.choice: Zone boundaries are level ± 1% of the CURRENT bar's Close, recomputed every bar
assumptions.reason: Spec explicitly parenthesizes 'level ±1% from Close', so the 1% is anchored to Close (dynamic per-bar), not to the level itself or to a fixed value at zone formation.

assumptions.choice: Deviated from canonical single-position defaults; implemented up to 3 concurrent 'units' as separate tracked entries, each with its own entry price, TP, and SL, partial-closed via sized buy()/sell() instead of self.close()
assumptions.reason: Spec explicitly requires 'no more than 3 open units' with TP/SL 'from the entry price', implying per-unit risk management (pyramiding), not a single netted position.

assumptions.choice: Per-unit order-ref tracking (entry_order_ref/exit_order_ref) in notify_order instead of a single pending-order flag
assumptions.reason: Multiple units can have entry or exit orders in flight simultaneously, so a single guard attribute would block valid concurrent unit activity that the spec requires.

assumptions.choice: TP/stop-loss/opposite-zone-close conditions are evaluated each bar against High/Low/Close in next(); when triggered, a default Market order is submitted for that unit's size (fills at the following bar's open)
assumptions.reason: Spec states price levels for TP/SL but not an order-type mechanism; using the same signal-then-next-bar-fill model as entries keeps execution timing internally consistent and matches the environment's default order behavior.

assumptions.topic: win-rate filter with no trade history
assumptions.choice: Treat the win-rate filter as satisfied (True) when trade_history is empty
assumptions.reason: Spec conditions entries on 'win rate >= 60% over the last 100 trades'; with zero closed trades there is no evidence against the filter, so it is not treated as blocking the first trades.

assumptions.choice: Per-unit win/loss determined from gross fill-price PnL (exit price vs entry price), excluding commission; last 100 closed units retained via a fixed-size deque
assumptions.reason: Backtrader's built-in Trade objects track net-position lifecycles, which do not map onto independently tracked sub-position units, so PnL is computed manually from stored entry/exit fill prices.

assumptions.choice: No extra restriction beyond the shared 3-unit cap if a long unit remains open when a later bar's trend flip enables a short entry (or vice versa)
assumptions.reason: Spec caps 'open units' per instrument at 3 without restricting direction mix; SMA slope conditions for long/short entries are mutually exclusive per bar but a previously opened opposite-direction unit could still be open.
